prompt: Build the V8 phase/packaging carrier with a crankcase block and counterweights: two banks at 45 degrees, four crank phase groups 0/90/180/270, eight piston-and-rod sets on four shared crankpins, and one connected crankshaft. The block is one connected casting with a base plate, two main-bearing webs at y = -20 and +20 with journal bores, and a continuous top rail; the main-bearing fit is measured at both stations. Each crank throw carries counterweight material opposite its pin on the declared web planes. All eighteen instances must export separately and must not interfere at the five listed input angles.
notes: Contract v4 (block/bearing/counterweight rung): the frame is a crankcase block with two main-bearing webs at y = -20 / +20, journal bores and a continuous top rail; each crank throw carries a counterweight lobe opposite the pin on its web planes.

The measured bearing fit binds the block bore to the crankshaft journals at the two declared stations, requiring the whole sampled clearance interval inside 0.4-1.6 mm and the measured axis offset at most 0.3 mm. This is a demonstrator clearance band, not a calibrated manufacturing tolerance, bearing load rating, lubrication or wear model.

Counterweight balance is a geometric vertex-sector measurement on the declared web planes: material beyond 10 mm on the pin side fails, and material opposite the throw must reach at least 12 mm within a 35-degree sector. It is not a mass moment, balance factor, stress or fatigue calculation.
Connectivity is exact edge connectivity of the rendered crank and block parts at 0 degrees; it is not balance, strength, machining or a complete cylinder block.

No cylinder bores, cylinder heads or firing order are modeled. Only five input angles, mesh-bounds slider centres, 153 pairwise collision checks per angle, two bearing stations and eight web planes are covered.
